Measurable Omega with finite measure mu and filtration F; scalar Brownian process B; scalar progressive L² integrand eta; its completed Ito integral I. A finite nondecreasing time list and its sum of squared integral increments.

T>0 is nonnegative real. B,eta,I:[0,infinity)×Omega→R. lambda_T is Lebesgue measure on [0,T] represented on nonnegative reals; product measure is mu⊗lambda_T. n∈N and times:{0,...,n}→[0,infinity).

Assumptions: eta is strongly progressive for F and (omega,r)↦eta(r,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). B satisfies standard scalar Brownian finite-dimensional distributions: for every finite nonnegative time set S, (B_s)_{s∈S} has centered Gaussian law with covariance (s,t)↦min(s,t), and B has continuous paths mu-a.e. In particular B_0=0 is required almost surely, not for every sample, is strongly adapted to F, and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for every s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. The time list is nondecreasing, not necessarily strictly increasing; its final value is at most T.

Conclusion: I is the specified continuous completed Ito integral of eta against B: the canonical elementary-integral limit off its null uniform-Cauchy exceptional set, zero on that set, and constant after T. Let S(omega)=∑_{r=0}^{n-1}(I(times_{r+1},omega)-I(times_r,omega))². Then S is mu-integrable and ∫S dmu=∫_{Omega×[times_0,times_n)} eta(v,omega)² d(mu⊗lambda_T)(omega,v).

Quantifier order: For every filtered finite measure setup, eta and Brownian B satisfying assumptions, and every n and nondecreasing list with times_n≤T, the squared-increment sum is integrable and has the stated integral.

Scope: Exact second-moment sum identity for any finite monotone partition, including repeated nodes, n=0 and a starting node different from zero. Time restriction is [times_0,times_n).

Constant dependencies: No existential constants or rates.
